name: Path decompositions of three fixed connected graphs (Gallai's conjecture)
description: construct() -> three lists of paths (vertex lists), one per fixed instance graph generated by instance_graph(n, p, seed) for (20,0.3,1), (25,0.3,2), (30,0.25,3) in the verifier. Paths must be simple, use graph edges, be edge-disjoint and cover all edges. Minimize the total number of paths; Gallai's conjecture predicts at most 10+13+15 = 38. The score is the total number of paths over three fixed random connected graphs; staying within 38 is consistent with the conjecture, exceeding it is not evidence against it.

sources.locator: Marthe Bonamy and Thomas J. Perrett, Gallai's path decomposition conjecture for graphs of small maximum degree (2019). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #583 page inspected: every connected graph on n vertices is conjectured to decompose into at most ceil(n/2) edge-disjoint paths (Erdős-Gallai); known for maximum degree <= 5, planar and 2-degenerate graphs, among other classes. The score is the total number of paths over three fixed random connected graphs; staying within 38 is consistent with the conjecture, exceeding it is not evidence against it.
Erdős Problem #583 (open (falsifiable)); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.
